ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a transition-state structure, with an Al atom at the upper left; Al is connected to two R groups, one H, and one O; O is connected below to the carbonyl/carbonyl position of the organic fragment. On the right side there is R1, and at the lower left there is an alkynyl fragment containing C≡C and connected to R. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: According to the specified method, divide the structure into the part around Al and the organic fragment to count non-hydrogen bonds. Around Al, Al–H is not counted, and two Al–R bonds and one Al–O bond are counted, for a total of 3. Then count the organic fragment: the O–C connection, the C–R1 connection, the C–C connection from the carbonyl carbon to the alkynyl carbon, the C≡C alkyne bond connection, and the terminal C–R connection, for a total of 5. Altogether 3 + 5 = 8 non-hydrogen bonds.
